calls.title: Experimentation Culture Award - Khan Academy
calls.summary: The team is developing a strong application for an AI and experimentation culture award, aiming for finalist status by utilizing existing content, including a 350-word summary. Kelli Hill noted abundant resources from past presentations and a recent blog post to support the application. Under Tushar Udeshi's leadership, a significant cultural shift has occurred at Khan Academy, encouraging experimentation and yielding notable improvements, such as a 10% rise in Next Item correctness. Ongoing collaboration with Anthropic and other AI providers aims to enhance tutoring models while maintaining cost-effectiveness through multi-model testing. Additionally, a strong portfolio of content, including a forthcoming paper, supports outreach efforts while team dynamics are bolstered by recent in-person offsites.
calls.keywords: Experimentation Culture, A/B Testing, AI Tutor, Cognitive Engagement, Growth Book, Anthropic
calls.action_items:
**Kelli Hill**
Submit the Experimentation Culture Award application after drafting it, including answering administrative questions such as organization size (15:30)

**Ashley Stirrup**
Draft the initial application summary for the Experimentation Culture Award using meeting notes, podcast, and blog post materials, then share with Khan Academy team for review and edits (15:30)
Provide guidance on crafting the 350-word description and effective presentation of Khan Academy's case for the Experimentation Culture Award (15:30)
Check if Drew Bent from Anthropic is included in the relevant Slack channel to facilitate ongoing collaboration on AI tutor improvements (13:40)

**All Participants**
Review and collaboratively edit the draft award submission after initial draft circulation to ensure accuracy and compelling presentation (15:30)
